title: Observation Schema
$comment: metadata is persisted as-is by the backend. correlation_ids and prompt_reference are dedicated top-level fields — structured platform data must use them, never metadata sub-keys.

input_tokens.description: DISJOINTNESS CONVENTION: EXCLUDES cache_read_tokens. Providers disagree natively -- Bedrock reports cache reads disjointly from inputTokens while OpenAI reports them as a SUBSET of prompt_tokens -- so producers normalize to the disjoint convention before emitting this field. A consumer multiplying this by a rate is pricing FRESH input only and must price cache_read_tokens separately at the cache-read rate. Records emitted before this contract lands may carry the provider-native convention and are NOT distinguishable by this field alone; see the 5.8.0 CHANGELOG entry.

cost_usd_declared.description: Cost the caller declared for this observation; null when none was declared. Stored alongside cost_usd_computed; never overwritten by the server.

cost_usd_computed.description: Cost the server computed from its price catalogue; null unless cost_status is priced.

priced_cost_usd.description: Sum of the priced token classes only. Equals cost_usd_computed when cost_status is priced; a lower bound ("at least") when partial; null when unpriced or not_applicable.

priced_model.description: Canonical model id of the price row used, or null when none was.

price_catalogue_version.description: Version of the price catalogue that produced cost_usd_computed / priced_cost_usd, or null.

input_data.description: Raw user-supplied input payload for this observation (e.g. the prompt sent to the model/tool). Unconstrained JSON.

output_data.description: Raw model/tool output payload for this observation. Unconstrained JSON.

metadata.description: Opaque user-supplied annotations. Do NOT place structured platform data here — correlation_ids and prompt_reference are dedicated top-level fields, never sub-keys of metadata.
